questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Production data shows that in 8% of cases your agent skips `get_customer` and calls `lookup_order` using only the customer's stated name, occasionally leading to misidentified accounts and incorrect refunds. What change most **effectively** addresses this?

options.text: Add a programmatic prerequisite blocking `lookup_order` and `process_refund` until `get_customer` has returned a verified customer ID.
Enhance the system prompt to state customer verification is mandatory before any order operations.
Add few-shot examples showing the agent always calling `get_customer` first.
Implement a routing classifier that enables only the relevant tool subset per request type.

questions.why: Deterministic compliance → prerequisite gate; B/C probabilistic; D addresses availability not ordering.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Your agent calls `get_customer` for order queries ("check my order #12345") instead of `lookup_order`. Both tools have minimal descriptions ("Retrieves customer information" / "Retrieves order details"). What's the most **effective first step**?

options.text: Add 5–8 few-shot examples to the system prompt for order queries.
Expand each tool's description with input formats, example queries, edge cases, and boundaries explaining when to use it vs alternatives.
Implement a routing layer that parses input and pre-selects the tool.
Consolidate into a single `lookup_entity` tool accepting any identifier.

questions.why: Tool descriptions are the primary selection mechanism; few-shot/routing/consolidation are over-engineering or root-cause misses for "first step."

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: FCR is 55% (target 80%). Logs show it escalates straightforward cases while autonomously handling complex policy-exception cases. Most effective way to improve escalation **calibration**?

options.text: Add explicit escalation criteria with few-shot examples demonstrating when to escalate vs resolve.
Have the agent self-report a confidence score (1–10); route below threshold to humans.
Deploy a classifier trained on historical tickets to predict escalations.
Sentiment analysis → auto-escalate when negative sentiment exceeds a threshold.

questions.why: Explicit criteria + few-shot is the proportionate first response; B/C/D are unreliable/over-engineered.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: A customer immediately replies "I want to speak to a human" before any investigation. The issue is a routine return within policy. What should the agent do?

options.text: Investigate first since the issue is clearly within capability; escalate only if resolution fails.
Acknowledge the request, but proceed to resolve because FCR is the priority.
Escalate immediately to a human agent.
Ask the customer to confirm three times before honoring the request.

questions.why: Honor explicit human-agent request **immediately**; don't gate on FCR.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: `lookup_order` returns five customer matches for "John Smith." What's correct behavior?

options.text: Select the most recent match by last-order date.
Choose the account with the highest lifetime value.
Ask the customer for additional identifiers to disambiguate.
Process a partial refund on the first match and ask for clarification.

questions.why: Ask for additional identifiers; heuristic selection is forbidden.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Business policy: refunds above $500 must always go to a human. Production shows the agent occasionally processes >$500 refunds. Best fix?

options.text: Add stronger wording in the system prompt about the $500 limit.
Implement a tool-call interception hook that blocks `process_refund` above $500 and redirects to `escalate_to_human`.
Increase the model's reasoning across retry attempts.

questions.why: Programmatic hook = guarantee for the >$500 policy; prompt is probabilistic.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Your agent must aggregate `get_customer`/`lookup_order` outputs from different MCP tools with inconsistent formats (Unix timestamps, ISO 8601, numeric codes). Where should normalization happen?

options.text: In the system prompt instructing the agent to interpret formats.
In a PostToolUse hook that normalizes tool results before the agent processes them.
By rewriting each backend to return a single canonical format.
By asking the model to detect format and convert during reasoning.

questions.why: PostToolUse hook normalizes before model sees results; deterministic across heterogeneous tools.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: During escalation, the human agent lacks access to the conversation transcript. What must the handoff include?

options.text: A link to the full transcript.
Customer ID, root cause analysis, refund amount (if any), and recommended action.
The agent's full internal reasoning trace.

questions.why: Self-contained handoff: ID + root cause + amount + recommended action.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: A message: "I want to return my last order, dispute a billing charge, and update my email." Best agent behavior?

options.text: Handle one at a time in the order received, ignoring the others until the first resolves.
Decompose into distinct items; investigate each (often in parallel, shared context); synthesize a unified resolution.
Route the entire message to `escalate_to_human` since it's multi-concern.
Process only the return; ignore the rest as out of scope.

questions.why: Decompose → investigate (parallel, shared) → synthesize unified resolution.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: What `stop_reason` value causes the agentic loop to **continue**?
questions.why: `tool_use` continues the loop.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Which is an anti-pattern for controlling the agentic loop?

options.text: Appending `tool_result` blocks to conversation history between iterations.
Parsing the assistant's natural-language text for the word "done" to decide termination.

questions.why: Parsing NL text for "done" is an explicit anti-pattern.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Which two are appropriate escalation triggers? (select exactly 2)

options.text: The customer explicitly requests a human.
The customer uses several exclamation marks.
The agent cannot make meaningful progress after reasoning + tools.
The case is routine and fully within policy.

questions.why: Explicit human request and inability to progress are valid triggers. (B sentiment, D routine = wrong.)

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Why is self-reported confidence score an unreliable escalation signal?

options.text: LLM self-confidence is poorly calibrated, especially on hard cases.
It can't be implemented in the Agent SDK.
Customers can see the score and get confused.

questions.why: Self-confidence poorly calibrated, especially hard cases.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Where must tool results be placed for the model to incorporate new information between iterations?

options.text: In a separate external log only.
Appended to conversation history as `tool_result` blocks (matched to `tool_use_id`).

questions.why: Append `tool_result` to history matched to `tool_use_id`.

questions.scenario: Scenario A — Customer Support Resolution Agent (Q1–15)
questions.text: Long sessions start giving inconsistent answers and citing "typical patterns." What's the best remedy?

options.text: Maintain scratchpad files of key findings and reference them for subsequent questions.
Re-summarize the entire history more aggressively.
Restart the loop on each user message.

questions.why: Scratchpad files counteract context degradation. (Bigger model/re-summarize = wrong.)

questions.text: For "impact of AI on creative industries," only visual arts coverage; coordinator decomposed into digital art, graphic design, photography. Root cause?

options.text: Coordinator's task decomposition is too narrow, omitting music/writing/film.
Web search queries aren't comprehensive enough.
Document analysis filtered out non-visual sources.

questions.why: Coordinator's narrow decomposition; subagents worked correctly within scope.

questions.text: Web search subagent times out. Which error propagation best enables intelligent recovery?

options.text: Structured error context: failure type + attempted query + partial results + alternative approaches.
Auto-retry with exponential backoff; return generic "search unavailable" after exhaustion.
Catch timeout, return empty result set marked as successful.
Propagate exception to a top-level handler that terminates the workflow.

questions.why: Structured error context enables recovery.

questions.text: Synthesis needs fact-checks in 85% simple cases (dates/names) and 15% deep investigations; routing all via coordinator adds 40% latency. Best approach?

options.text: Give synthesis a scoped `verify_fact` tool for simple lookups; complex cases delegate via coordinator.
Give synthesis all web search tools.
Have web search proactively cache context anticipating needs.

questions.why: Scoped tool = principle of least privilege; preserve pattern for complex cases.

questions.text: For the coordinator to spawn subagents, what must its config include?

options.text: A "coordinator" role in the system prompt.

questions.why: `Task` in `allowedTools` is required to spawn subagents.

questions.text: Do subagents inherit the coordinator's conversation history?

options.text: No — context is isolated; everything must be passed explicitly in the prompt.
Only for the first three turns.

questions.why: Isolated context; explicit passing only.

questions.text: To run subagents in parallel, the coordinator should:

options.text: Emit one Task call per turn across multiple turns.
Emit multiple Task tool calls in a single coordinator response.
Use a higher concurrency limit setting.

questions.why: Multiple Task calls in a single response.

questions.text: How should the coordinator's prompt be structured for best subagent adaptability?
questions.why: Goals + quality criteria enable adaptability.

questions.text: Conflicting credible statistics appear in two sources. Synthesis should:

options.text: Pick the more recent publication regardless of source quality.
Include both values with explicit source attribution; mark as contested.

questions.why: Annotate conflict with attribution; don't pick arbitrarily.

questions.text: Subagent outputs must include which for temporal correctness during synthesis?
questions.why: Publication/collection dates prevent temporal differences being misread as contradictions.

questions.text: Synthesis should render content types how?

options.text: Convert everything to a uniform bullet list.
Render appropriately: financial → tables, news → prose, technical → structured lists.

questions.why: Render types appropriately; don't unify.

questions.text: What should the synthesis pass include when some sources were unavailable?

options.text: Coverage annotations indicating well-supported vs gap areas.
Removal of the affected section silently.

questions.why: Coverage annotations flag well-supported vs gaps.

questions.text: Refinement loop in multi-agent research:

options.text: Coordinator evaluates synthesis for gaps; re-delegates targeted queries; re-invokes synthesis until coverage sufficient.
Always run three independent synthesis passes and pick the best.
Restart the entire pipeline from scratch on any gap.
Skip gap evaluation to save latency.

questions.why: Coordinator's iterative refinement on gaps.

questions.text: Why structure subagent outputs (separating content from metadata like URLs/page numbers)?

options.text: To preserve attribution/source provenance when passing between agents.

questions.why: Preserve attribution/provenance when passing between agents.

questions.text: When downstream subagents have limited context budgets, what should upstream agents do?

options.text: Return structured data (key facts, citations, relevance scores) instead of verbose content.
Send only the most recent message.

questions.why: Return structured data not verbose content for limited downstream budgets.

questions.text: Best use of `fork_session` in research?

options.text: Create parallel branches from a shared analysis baseline to explore divergent approaches.

questions.why: `fork_session` = branches from shared baseline.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: CI job: `claude "Analyze this PR for security issues"` hangs waiting for input. Correct approach?
questions.why: `-p` (`--print`) = non-interactive; others are non-existent.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: Manager proposes switching BOTH a blocking pre-merge check and an overnight debt report to Message Batches (50% off). How to evaluate?

options.text: Batch for the debt report only; real-time for the blocking pre-merge.
Switch both to batch with status polling.
Keep both real-time to avoid ordering issues.
Switch both to batch with a real-time timeout fallback.

questions.why: Batch for overnight (no SLA); sync for blocking pre-merge.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: 14-file PR produces inconsistent depth + contradictory feedback (flag a pattern in one file, approve identical code elsewhere). Restructure how?

options.text: Per-file local analysis pass + separate cross-file integration pass.
Require devs to split PRs into 3–4 files.
Use a higher-tier model with a bigger context window.
Run 3 independent full-PR passes; flag issues in ≥2.

questions.why: Per-file + integration passes fix attention dilution.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: Best mechanism for machine-parseable findings to post as inline PR comments?
questions.why: `--output-format json` + `--json-schema` for structured CI output.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: Avoid duplicate review comments when re-running after new commits:

options.text: Include prior findings in context; instruct Claude to report only new/unaddressed issues.
Use a different model each time.

questions.why: Include prior findings → only new/unaddressed.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: Generated tests duplicate existing test scenarios. Best fix?

options.text: Provide existing test files in context + document testing standards/fixtures in CLAUDE.md.
Generate tests only for new files.

questions.why: Provide existing tests + standards/fixtures in CLAUDE.md.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: Review of generated code — best practice?

options.text: Same Claude session that generated the code reviews it.
Use an independent Claude instance (no prior reasoning context).
Ask the generator to "be extra careful."
Add extended thinking to the same session.

questions.why: Independent instance > self-review.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: Review FP rate is high in the "documentation accuracy" category, damaging trust. Proportionate first response?

options.text: Define explicit categorical criteria ("flag only when claimed behavior contradicts actual code") and improve prompts for that category.

questions.why: Explicit criteria + improve prompts; proportionate response.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: "Be conservative; only report high-confidence findings" — effective for precision?

options.text: No — specific categorical criteria outperform vague confidence-based filtering.

questions.why: Vague "be conservative" fails vs specific criteria.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: Which CLAUDE.md CLI/context measures improve CI test-generation quality? (select exactly 2)

options.text: Document testing standards, valuable criteria, and fixtures in CLAUDE.md.
Provide existing test files in context.

questions.why: Document standards in CLAUDE.md + provide existing tests. (C/D wrong.)

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: Message Batches API supports multi-turn tool calling within a single request?

options.text: No — it does not support multi-turn tool calling mid-request.

questions.why: Batches: no multi-turn tool calling within a request.

questions.scenario: Scenario C — Claude Code for Continuous Integration (Q31–42)
questions.text: To guarantee overall SLA of 30 hours using Batches (≤24h processing), you should:

options.text: Submit batches at 4-hour intervals so a 24-hour batch still beats the 30-hour SLA.
Submit one batch and hope it's fast.

questions.why: Cadence ensures 24h max batch fits in 30h SLA.

questions.text: Most reliable way to guarantee schema-compliant structured output?

options.text: Free-text JSON with "output valid JSON only."
`tool_use` with a JSON schema as input parameters.

questions.why: `tool_use` + JSON schema = most reliable.

questions.text: `tool_choice` setting when document type is unknown and several extraction schemas exist?
questions.why: `"any"` guarantees a tool call; choose which.

questions.text: To force `extract_metadata` to run before enrichment tools:

options.text: Put `extract_metadata` first in the system prompt.

questions.why: Forced tool_choice then follow-up turns.

questions.text: A field may legitimately be absent from some source documents. Best schema design?

options.text: Make all fields required and instruct the model to guess.
Make such fields optional/nullable so the model returns null rather than fabricating.

questions.why: Optional/nullable prevents fabrication.

questions.text: Best pattern for an extensible categorical field?

options.text: Enum with "other" + a detail string (and "unclear" for ambiguous cases).

questions.why: Enum + "other" + detail; "unclear" for ambiguity.

questions.text: Validation failed: line items don't sum to the stated total. Retry strategy?

options.text: Append the original document, the failed extraction, and the specific validation errors to the prompt and retry.
Retry with no changes until it passes.

questions.why: Retry with original doc + failed extraction + specific errors.

questions.text: When is retry-with-error-feedback **ineffective**?

options.text: When the formatting mismatch is the issue.
When the required information is simply absent from the source document.
When the schema has optional fields.

questions.why: Ineffective when info absent from source.

questions.text: To catch semantic errors (sum mismatch, wrong field), best design?

options.text: Add computed cross-checks like `calculated_total` vs `stated_total`, `conflict_detected` booleans.

questions.why: Computed cross-checks catch semantic errors.

questions.text: Review a 100-doc batch result: aggregate accuracy is 97%, but you suspect weak segments. Best verification?

options.text: Stratified random sampling; analyze accuracy by document type and field.

questions.why: Stratified sampling + segment by type/field detects masked poor segments.

questions.text: Routing rule for human review (limited capacity):

options.text: Route low-confidence OR ambiguous/contradictory-source extractions to human review, prioritizing capacity.

questions.why: Route low-confidence/ambiguous to humans, prioritizing capacity.

questions.text: CLAUDE.md hierarchy from highest to lowest precedence:

options.text: Enterprise managed → user (`~/.claude/`) → project (`./` or `.claude/`) → directory.

questions.why: Managed → user → project → directory.

questions.text: A new team member doesn't receive coding conventions you wrote. Diagnosis?

options.text: The conventions are in user-level config, not shared via version control — move to project-level.

questions.why: User-level not shared via VCS; move to project-level.

questions.text: Best mechanism to enforce that test-file conventions apply to `*.test.tsx` files scattered across the repo?

options.text: A skill that loads on demand.

questions.why: `.claude/rules/` with `paths:` globs handles scattered files.

questions.text: You want a verbose codebase-analysis skill not to pollute the main conversation. Frontmatter?
questions.why: `context: fork` isolates skill output.

questions.text: Find all callers of `processRefund` across the codebase. Tool?
questions.why: Grep = content search.

questions.text: Find all test files anywhere in the repo. Tool?
questions.why: Glob = path search.

questions.text: You try to `Edit` a common string that appears 12 times. Correct fallback?

options.text: Read the full file, then Write the modified content.

questions.why: Read + Write fallback for non-unique Edit.

questions.text: Which is OUT OF SCOPE for the exam (per the Exam Guide)?
questions.why: MCP hosting/containers explicitly out-of-scope.
